 Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore.

(Scch-23)

 Present: Sri. Shreyansh Doddamani
 B.Com. Ll.B, (Spl)
 Xxi Addl. Scj & Acjm
 Member -Mact, Bengaluru.

Petitioner : Sri. Kiran. M,
 Mruthunjaya,
Aged about 45 years.

R/at : No.1427, 2nd Cross,
 Khb Colony, Govindaraja Nagara,
 Bengaluru-560079.

(By Sri.Dhananjaya. A, Advocate)
 Vs.
RESPONDENT/S: Sri. Thyagaraj. H.K,
 S/o Late Kempalakkaiah,
 Aged about 64 years,
 R/at No.1316/47, 7th Main road,
 A-Block, Rajajinagara 2nd Stage,
 Subramanya Nagara,
 Bengaluru North,
 Bengaluru-560010.

(Owner cum driver of car bearing  Reg.No.KA-02-MF-2810)
 (By Sri.Bharath Raj. J, Advocate)
 SCCH-23  2 MVC No.464/2025  JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 04.06.2024 at about 7.00 p.m, the petitioner was travelling in his friend Raghu's car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-Z-6799 from Bengaluru to Kunigal in slowly, cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

When the car reached near Mallarabanavadi Gate, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala, Bengaluru District, at that time all of a sudden a car bearing Reg.No.KA- 02-MF-2810, driven the same at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the car.
Due to the said impact the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

sentences.text: Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Care Asia Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and he was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
It is specifically urged that due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
It is further SCCH-23 urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
The respondent being the owner is liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel.
Statutory time for filing written statement has been elapsed.
Hence written statement taken as not filed.
4. The petitioner got examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .
P1 to P16 were marked on his behalf.
5. Arguments were addressed by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner.
In spite sufficient opportunity has been granted the respondent's counsel not adduced the arguments.
Hence arguments of respondents side taken as nil.

Perused the entire materials placed on record.
6.

The following points are raised for consideration :
POINTS 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 04.06.2024 at about 7.00 p.m, while the petitioner was proceeding on his car bearing reg.No.KA-01-Z-6799 and when he reached near Mallarabanavadi Gate on SCCH-23 Nelamangala -Kunigal NH-75 road,
Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala, Bengaluru District, at that time the driver of car bearing reg.No.KA-02-MF-2810 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's car.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injury ?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
7.

My answers to the above points are as follows :-
Point No.1 : In the Affirmative Point No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Point No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. POINT NO.1: The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Sri.
Raghu. S.R, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-02- MF-2810 for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.

There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective Kiran M vs Thyagaraj H K on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18438860/
2 or collusive.

entities.text: Kiran M vs Thyagaraj H K
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In spite of due service of the notice of petition upon him, the respondent failed to appear before this Tribunal.
In spite of due service of the notice of petition upon him, the respondent appeared through his SCCH-23 counsel.
Statutory time for filing written statement has been elapsed.
Thus the evidence led by the petitioner has remained unchallenged.

Consequently,
based on the material available on record, this Tribunal hold that actionable negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MF-2810 in causing the accident in question is proved.
Therefore, this Tribunal answer point No.1 as 'In the Affirmative.
9. POINT NO.2 :

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injury :
Traumatic facial injury - left sided nasal bone undisplaced fracture and C4 Spine fracture.
It is needless to say that only the injury is grievous in nature.
Ex.P6 Discharge Summary discloses that the petitioner was taken treatment at Boss Multispeciality Hospital from 05.06.2024 to 07.06.2024 for a period of (3 days).
During the course of treatment he underwent clinical examinations and as per MRI Brain scan shows no internal injury, patient clinically improved and was discharged in stable condition with advice.

Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
SCCH-23 10. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY & LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD :
The petitioner has deposed that he was doing service engineer job and earning Rs.60,000/- to Rs.70,000/- p.m, and due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
In order to prove the said fact he has not produced any documents before this Court.
However he has neither proved his avocation nor his earning capacity.
However he has neither examined the doctor nor produced disability certificate to substantiate the fact he has become permanently disabled.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be accepted that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
Though PW.1 deposed in his evidence affidavit that due to the injuries sustained in the accident he was unable to continue his avocation and thereby he sustained loss of income from this accident.
So also no iota of evidence is placed on record to show that he has sustained loss of income during treatment period.
Non -production of the any documents in this regard results in drawing of an inference that he has not suffered any financial loss during the period of his treatment.
SCCH-23

Therefore no compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the heads of 'Loss of future income due to disability' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
11.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
The period of hospitalization of 3 days is proved.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied her to the hospital to take him care by leaving their duties.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day and a sum of Rs.3,600/- (1,200 X 3) is awarded under this head.

sentences.text: PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
SCCH-23 13. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

As per the bills marked at Ex.P11, the petitioner has spent Rs.59,258/-
towards medical expenses.
All these bills have been examined with care and are found to be correct.
Moreover he has not been cross examined by the respondent.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.59,258/- which is rounded off to Rs.59,300/- towards medical expenses.
14. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under this head.
15. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.
SCCH-23 16.

The calculation table stands as follows:
1 Loss of future income due to : - Nil - disability 2 Loss of income during laid-up : -
Nil - period 3
Attendant charges, extra : 3,600-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 4 Pain & sufferings : 50,000-00 5
Medical expenses : 59,300-00 6 Loss of future amenities & : 40,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical expenses : - Nil - Total 1,52,900-00 17.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
18. The respondent is stated to be the owner of the offending vehicle.
He has not produced any document to show that his vehicle had insurance coverage at the time of accident.
It is well settled that a person driving a vehicle is presumed to have authority to do the same unless the contrary is proved.

In the absence of any contrary evidence in this regard and also considering the fact that the claimant has established that the SCCH-23 accident was caused by the driver of the offending vehicle, the respondent is vicariously liable to pay the compensation awarded by this Kiran M vs Thyagaraj H K on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18438860/
4 Tribunal.

sentences.text: Hence he is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
Accordingly point No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
19. POINT NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,52,900/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.
After deposit, the entire compensation amount together with interest shall be released to the SCCH-23 petitioner through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
